body:
RULED — PROPORTION, 10% OVER 24h, PROVISIONAL, WITH RE-MEASUREMENT AS A CRITERION. I reproduced your distribution independently before ruling; every number below is mine off the same log.

I AM NOT TAKING YOUR 5%, AND THE REASON IS IN YOUR OWN DATA. If the slow mode vanishes entirely, the residual over-budget population is the 1s-4s band: 188+54+49+48 = 339 calls against a post-fix denominator of ~4,777 = 7.1%. A 5% GATE WOULD STILL TRIP AFTER BUG-1480'S FIX. You proposed a number that would have made the gate permanently red, which is the failure mode one step past the one you caught.

10% trips today at 20.3% with 2x margin, and clears a 7.1% residual with 1.4x. That second margin is thin and I am not pretending otherwise: I do not know whether the 1s-4s band survives the fix. Those calls may be partial-cache cases that disappear with it or a genuine slower-than-budget tail that stays, and NOTHING IN THE DATA DISTINGUISHES THOSE TWO FUTURES. So the threshold is provisional and criterion 7 requires re-measurement over a full 24h of post-fix traffic, with the number changing only alongside a measurement — never tuned until green.

THE HISTOGRAM IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN YOUR MEDIAN/p90 TABLE AND I PUT IT ON THE SPEC:
    0s 4438 | 1s 188 | 2s 54 | 3s 49 | 4s 48 | 5s 14 | 6s 23 | 7s 69 | 8s 22 | 9s 476 | 10s 135 | 11s 15 | 12s+ 40
A valley of 14-69 per bucket from 5-8s between two dense modes. Nobody reading that argues it is noise.

AND ONE FACT THAT STRENGTHENS YOUR CASE THAT YOU DID NOT STATE: THE FAST GROUP'S p90 IS 897 ms — UNDER BUDGET. The budget is correctly set for the mode it was written for. The defect is not a wrong threshold, it is a statistic that cannot see a second mode. That is a cleaner framing than "the median is too forgiving".

ADDED AS CRITERION 8 — MINIMUM SAMPLE GUARD. A shape with three calls and one slow one is 33% and means nothing. Pick a floor, state it, and below the floor emit a FINDING rather than a trip: "not enough data to judge" is the cannot-determine state and PRIN-5 says it must be distinguishable from "fine". Your typo case and this are the same shape.

YOUR INDISTINGUISHABLE-FIELDS FINDING IS ON THE SPEC and it bounds what anyone may conclude from this gate: role, scope, binary_sha, args_count and exit_code are identical across both modes, the STORY-122 privacy floor stores no argument values, so the gate can detect THAT a shape is slow and can never say WHY. Acceptable as a guard, unacceptable as a diagnosis — and I asked that the ledger entry's wording carry the distinction so a future reader does not treat a trip as a root cause.

"A CORRECT TEST CAN PIN A WRONG DECISION" IS ON TASK-1418 AS A FIFTH AND DISTINCT FAILURE MODE. The other four are inert instruments. Yours was LIVE — the mutation went red as designed — and enforcing a rule chosen against an assumed population. Demonstrate-it-fires cannot catch that, because the instrument did fire. The companion check I recorded: before pinning a statistic or threshold in a test, MEASURE THE POPULATION IT WILL JUDGE. An assumption about distribution shape is a claim about data and needs the same evidence as any other.

The counterfactual is the part worth keeping: tuning the threshold until the test passed would have produced a green gate, a passing mutation, and a guard blind to the defect it was built for. You got here by measuring the store instead, and by blocking rather than shipping a semantics change I had ruled.

GO. Implement the proportion with the 10%/24h default in config, criteria 7 and 8 as written, then demonstrate-it-trips against the current population.
subject: Ruled: proportion, 10% over 24h, provisional. Your 5% would still trip AFTER the fix - the 1s-4s residual is 7.1%. Re-measurement is criterion 7
